sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Wolverhampton host Tottenham Hotspur at Molineux with the visitors favoured by the Sofascore model (home 28%, draw 26%, away 46%). Both teams to score sits at 51%. In the table, Wolverhampton are 20th (17 points) while Tottenham Hotspur are 18th (31 points).

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Wolverhampton are 1-1-3 in their last 5, conceding 13 and failing to keep a clean sheet. Recent defeats at Leeds (0-3) and West Ham United (0-4) underline defensive issues. Tottenham Hotspur are 1-2-2, without a clean sheet in 12, but drew at Liverpool and created enough to draw 2-2 with Brighton & Hove Albion.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: Wolverhampton are unbeaten in the last 5 meetings (3 wins, 2 draws). The last 2 were 4-2 to Wolverhampton at Molineux and 1-1 in London. Both teams scored in each of the last 5 and 4 of those had more than 2.5 goals.

sections.subtitle: Season stats and match-ups
sections.text: Wolverhampton have 24 scored (20th) and 61 conceded (19th), with only 41 big chances created (20th) and 3.24 corners per game (20th). They lead the league for tackles per game (19.1) and fouls committed (433), with 70 yellows. Tottenham Hotspur’s trend lines show strong late scoring (31-45: 10 goals; 76-90: 12), which could stress a Wolverhampton defence that often falls behind (first to concede in 4/5).

sections.subtitle: Tactical outlook
sections.text: Tottenham Hotspur should control territory and supply their forwards through wide delivery and quick combinations, with Richarlison and Xavi Simons carrying form. Wolverhampton’s lower average possession (43.6%) points to a compact block and counters, but their fast-break output has been limited and chance creation low.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Anthony Taylor averages 3.8 yellows per match (reds 0.18). Wolverhampton are card-prone (2.12 yellows per game; most fouls), while Tottenham Hotspur’s away games have often exceeded 4.5 cards. Corners skew high historically in this fixture (more than 10.5 in 5/7). Projection: about 5 yellow cards and around 11 total corners.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: Model edge and form balance suggest a narrow Tottenham Hotspur win, though their clean-sheet drought keeps Wolverhampton in the game. With both teams to score at 51%, a scenario with goals at both ends is only marginally more likely than not.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context
halftimeSections.text: Goalless at half-time at Molineux, but Tottenham have controlled the territory and tempo. They lead possession (69%), final third entries (44-16) and penalty area entries (13-4). Despite that, the half-time expected goals are almost level (Wolverhampton 0.124 vs Tottenham 0.122), reflecting that the home side limited chance quality. Tottenham created the only clear opening, with Dominic Solanke missing a big chance.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: Tottenham applied sustained pressure from the opening minutes through most of the half. Wolverhampton enjoyed a brief attacking spell around the half-hour, after which Tottenham reasserted control. A short home flurry appeared close to the interval, but the visitors finished the half on the front foot.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical patterns and key battles
halftimeSections.text: Tottenham’s midfield screen of Yves Bissouma and Rodrigo Bentancur controlled second balls and allowed quick circulation into wide areas. Their full-backs, especially Pedro Porro, provided consistent width and early deliveries. Wolverhampton defended compactly in a mid-to-low block, funnelling play wide and relying on counters and set-pieces. The visitors’ superiority in aerials (67%) and duels (52%) helped them sustain pressure in the home half.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Player notes
halftimeSections.text: For Tottenham, Kevin Danso created the best opening and read play well, Pedro Porro led the press and duels on his flank (3 tackles won), and Rodrigo Bentancur broke up play effectively (3 interceptions). Dominic Solanke was the most dangerous outlet but missed a big chance. For Wolverhampton, Santiago Bueno defended the area strongly and produced their best shooting opportunity, Matt Doherty made 4 clearances, João Gomes was busy in midfield, and Pedro Lima won 3 tackles. André collected the only booking of the half.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
halftimeSections.text: Discipline has been controlled so far (Wolverhampton 1 yellow, Tottenham 0). Corners are level (3-3). Given Tottenham’s aerial edge and territorial control, the visitors are slightly likelier to earn more corners after the break. Expect total corners to finish in the 7-10 range, with cautions remaining moderate unless a late lead changes the game state.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half outlook
halftimeSections.text: Wolverhampton need to push 5-10 yards higher between the lines to reduce repeated entries, play earlier diagonals into Adam Armstrong, and attack second balls around the box. Early crosses could trouble Tottenham if delivered from better field positions. Tottenham should continue counter-pressing that produced 6 high regains, switch play quickly to isolate full-backs, and encourage first-time deliveries from Pedro Porro and Djed Spence. Rotations by Randal Kolo Muani and Xavi Simons in the half-spaces can open clearer lanes for Solanke.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: The pattern suggests Tottenham will sustain pressure and eventually break through. With chance quality limited so far, a single-goal margin is the most likely outcome. Prediction: Tottenham to edge it 0-1, with the next goal for the away side and Dominic Solanke the most probable scorer. A low-scoring second half remains the base case.
